messages:
acme-chatops: Hey, heads up — since the 03/12 canary rollout our customer chatbot sometimes switches style/answers mid-conversation. Two examples attached (req ids below). Same user, back-to-back prompts, different model behavior (one verbose + policy-safe, then terse and omits required safety fallback). Causes a bad UX.

acme-chatops: SAMPLE 1: req_id=0e9d3f1a, prompt='How do I reset my API key?', model_response='You can go to Settings > API keys...' (normal)
acme-chatops: SAMPLE 2: req_id=0e9d3f1b, prompt='How do I reset my API key? I lost access to email', model_response='Just do it yourself.' (short/odd)

jessica: Sorry about this — can you confirm region and whether you're pinning a model in the request? Also pls paste the full request ids and any conversation_id so we can correlate. We'll escalate to eng.

acme-chatops: region=us-east-1, not pinning. We use conversation_id=conv_42 for the session. We see the switch inside the same conversation, same session headers. Both requests within ~2s of each other.

jessica: Copy, escalating to eng-ml. @ajay @nina assigning. Suspect routing->variant fallback during serving.

ajay: I pulled routing traces for those req ids. Quick summary: we have evidence of model-variant handoff for conv_42 due to transient capacity pressure + routing policy allowing fallback to quantized variants. Logs snippet below (redacted):

```
[2026-03-12T03:11:59Z] req=0e9d3f1a conv=conv_42 route=prod-us-east-1 model_variant=redwood-medium-2026q1 decision=serve
[2026-03-12T03:12:01Z] req=0e9d3f1b conv=conv_42 route=prod-us-east-1 model_variant=redwood-medium-q4-4bit decision=fallback reason=capacity_exhausted
```

ajay: The two responses were served by different runtime variants (full precision vs quantized 4-bit). That explains the abrupt change in verbosity/safety handling. Our routing currently allows fallback to quantized variants when latency/capacity tradeoffs trigger. We should have session-stickiness to avoid intra-conversation variant flips.

acme-chatops: Oof. Is there a quick workaround? Customer wants consistent answers ASAP.

ajay: Short-term options:
- Pin model_variant in the API call: {"model_variant":"redwood-medium-2026q1"} — forces the same binary for the session.
- Use header X-Redwood-Variant-Sticky: true (temporary testing header) — pins variant for conversation_id for 1 hour.
- Disable fallback for your project via console: Project -> Serving -> Routing -> disable "allow_quantized_fallback" (we can do this for your org).

ajay: Example curl to force variant for repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "X-Redwood-Force-Variant: redwood-medium-2026q1" \
 -d '{"conversation_id":"conv_42","input":"How do I reset my API key?"}'
```

nina: Infra note: at ~03:12 UTC we saw a short spike in pod evictions in us-east-1 due to a noisy tenant on shared pool; autoscaler reacted and routing picked quantized variants as fallback to preserve latency SLOs. I temporarily increased reserved capacity for the customer's org and rolled a config change to set conversation pinning for their org while we triage.

jessica: Thanks, nina. I've informed the customer and applied the temporary pin for conv_42. Customer confirmed behavior normalized for subsequent messages.

ajay: Longer-term fix proposals:
1) Treat requests with the same conversation_id as variant-sticky by default for 24h to avoid mid-session flips.
2) Add routing invariant: disallow fallback to lower-quality quantized family if the exact semantics/safety profile is not verified for that model. Marked as P1 for eng-ml.
3) Add telemetry flag that surfaces "variant_change" events per conversation so we can auto-alert support.

acme-chatops: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please add us to the postmortem and keep us updated on the permanent fix timeline. Also we'll run a regression test suite with pinned variant to confirm.

jessica: Will do — assigning follow-ups: ENG-ML ticket #INF-3147 for variant-stickiness, SRE ticket #SRE-2029 for capacity isolation, and we'll send a short customer-facing incident note.

deploy-bot: deploy note: rollback of routing weight change completed at 2026-03-12T03:20:12Z for prod-us-east-1.

nina: Closing loop — I increased dedicated buffer for the org, routed additional capacity, and scheduled a capacity bump for next maintenance window. We'll sync with product on routing policy changes.

jessica: Thanks everyone. Customer reopened if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:
